methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Dual Component (Math + ELA)
content: Problem: In Phase 2, students must learn both hard academic concepts (Math/Logic) and the language to explain them (ELA), which can cause cognitive overload if taught simultaneously.

Solution: Every session is strictly split. Part 1 (Math Component, 40 mins) focuses purely on identifying patterns, rules, and sequences using detective logic. Part 2 (ELA Component, 80 mins) shifts to the grammatical structures ("must be" + sequence words) needed to explain the logic step-by-step.

parts.title: PART 1: MATH COMPONENT
content: A. Math Reading Input: The Secret Door
Max is a smart detective (thám tử). He finds a secret door. It has a lock (ổ khóa). The lock shows a strange code: Circle, Square, Triangle, Circle, Square...
"There is a missing shape!" says Max. "I must find the rule (quy tắc). It is a repeating pattern (quy luật)."
Max uses his math brain. The shapes repeat in the same order again and again.
"Circle, Square, Triangle," Max says. "If the last shape was a Square, what is next?"
→ Memory trick: P-A-T: Pay Attention Today
b. Look at the _______________ on the door.
→ Memory trick: R-E-P: Read Every Pattern
→ Key Collocation: repeat again and again
→ Memory trick: M-I-S-S: Must Investigate Secret Spaces
→ Memory trick: N-E-X-T: Now Exactly X Times

parts.title: PART 2: ELA COMPONENT
content: A. ELA Reading Input: Using Logic
Max writes the sequence in his notebook to solve the puzzle (câu đố).

Max looks at the lock. "The last shape is a square. Therefore, the next shape must be a triangle!"

Pip the squirrel has a big wooden box for his winter acorns. The box has a number lock. Pip sees a sequence (chuỗi) of numbers: 2, 4, 6, 8...
